tests.name: test_filled
tests.description: proves and solves both give an answer, not None.

tests.name: test_true_sums
tests.description: proves gives True for the triangle numbers, the squares, the cubes and the odd numbers.

tests.name: test_wrong_step
tests.description: proves gives False for n^2 as the sum 1 + 2 + ... + n, whose base case holds but whose step fails.

tests.name: test_wrong_base
tests.description: proves gives False for n(n + 1)(2n + 1)/6 + 1 as the sum of the squares: at n = 1 it is 2, not 1.
tests.message: proves(squares_plus_one, square) gives True, not False: at n = 1 it gives 2, not 1.

tests.name: test_tiles
tests.description: solves gives True for the tiles, (4^n - 1)/3 from T(0) = 0 with T(k + 1) = 4T(k) + 1, and False for 2^n - 1.

tests.name: test_average
tests.description: solves gives True for the running average 1 - 0.9^n from 0, and False for 1 - 0.9^(n + 1), which is one step out.
tests.message: solves(average_late, 0, smooth) gives True, not False: its step holds, but at n = 0 it gives 1/10, not 0.

tests.name: test_filled
tests.description: cover still returns a list, not None.

tests.name: test_two
tests.description: A grid 2 by 2 is covered by one tile, wherever its cut square is.
tests.message: cover(2, 0, 0, [0, 0]) has a tile [[0, 0], [0, 1], [1, 0], [1, 1]] with 4 squares, not 3. In each call, only the three quarters that do not hold that call's hole give the centre tile a square, and each of them is covered with that square left out.

tests.name: test_four
tests.description: A grid 4 by 4 is covered by 5 tiles, wherever its cut square is.
tests.message: cover(4, 0, 0, [0, 0]) has a tile [[0, 0], [0, 1], [1, 0], [1, 1]] with 4 squares, not 3. In each call, only the three quarters that do not hold that call's hole give the centre tile a square, and each of them is covered with that square left out.

tests.name: test_eight
tests.description: A grid 8 by 8 is covered by 21 tiles, wherever its cut square is.
tests.message: cover(8, 0, 0, [0, 0]) has a tile [[0, 0], [0, 1], [1, 0], [1, 1]] with 4 squares, not 3. In each call, only the three quarters that do not hold that call's hole give the centre tile a square, and each of them is covered with that square left out.

tests.name: test_elsewhere
tests.description: A block whose top left square is not [0, 0] is covered inside its own edges.
tests.message: cover(4, 8, 16, [8, 16]) has a tile [[8, 16], [8, 17], [9, 16], [9, 17]] with 4 squares, not 3. In each call, only the three quarters that do not hold that call's hole give the centre tile a square, and each of them is covered with that square left out.

tests.name: test_sixty_four
tests.description: A grid 64 by 64 is covered by 1,365 tiles, which is (4^6 - 1) / 3, with the cut square in three places.
tests.message: cover(64, 0, 0, [37, 12]) has a tile [[0, 0], [0, 1], [1, 0], [1, 1]] with 4 squares, not 3. In each call, only the three quarters that do not hold that call's hole give the centre tile a square, and each of them is covered with that square left out.

tests.name: test_small
tests.description: power(x, n) is x^n for every integer x from -3 to 3 and every n from 0 to 12.

tests.name: test_odd
tests.description: Odd powers come out right: power(2, 3) is 8 and power(2, 5) is 32.

tests.name: test_large
tests.description: power(3, 5000) is 3^5000, a number with 2,386 digits, which halving reaches in a chain of 14 calls.
tests.message: power(3, 5000) is not 3 to the power 5,000.
